question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP
request.body: A single GET of the Help Center article search endpoint on the vendor's own instance, query 'resolution tiers', per_page 3. No credential, no cookie jar, no prior request on the connection, no custom User-Agent.

decoded.result: count 901, page_count 301, three results returned, each with title, html_url and the article's full body HTML
decoded.scope: this is one customer's public help centre, which happens to be the vendor's own; it is documented anonymous end-user access, not access to the Zendesk product
decoded.rate-limit: the response carries x-rate-limit 10000 and x-rate-limit-remaining 8781; whether an anonymous request draws that budget down is not established: the 12:06Z answer was a Cloudflare cache HIT, and a re-run of the published command at 18:04Z (section 6 of the artifact) answered the identical remaining value
decoded.not-measured: whether any other instance allows it, whether the limit is per IP or per instance, and anything requiring a credential
decoded.user-agent: the published command sends curl's default User-Agent; the 12:06Z request sent an unrecorded one, and the 18:04Z re-run with the default answered the same status and count, so the observation does not depend on it

finding: An agent with no account, no cookie and no key can search a Zendesk instance's help centre through the documented REST API and receive ranked articles with their full bodies: 901 matches for one query on the vendor's own instance. That is the documented anonymous end-user permission, not a gap, and it does not touch the product: the two jobs this entry claims for Zendesk both run inside an account. What it does establish is that the reference material behind a Zendesk help centre is machine-readable to a stranger, and that the response headers disclose the instance's rate-limit budget to the anonymous caller; whether the anonymous request is counted against it was not established.
